name: @onimaxxing/sussy-seeds-mcp

tools.name: listClusters
tools.description: Every cluster the game ships: coord prefix, English label, group (classic/spacedOut/lab), DLC requirements, menu order. Use this FIRST to resolve a user's cluster mention ('Marinea Minor', 'Terra', 'Ceres') to its coordinatePrefix. Entries whose English labels share a stem with another cluster (Marinea/Marinea-Minor, Ceres/Ceres-Minor, etc.) carry disambiguationHint + ambiguousWith fields so you never grab the wrong variant from an ambiguous user reference — read those fields when the user's cluster name is one word.

tools.name: listStoryTraits
tools.description: Every story trait the game ships, plus the mod-added story traits available through trait overlays. Stock traits: pick the id and include it in the CoordFormState.storyTraits array; each row's spawnTag is the EXACT prefab tag the trait places (use it as world.spawn's tagSubstring — the yaml id often differs from the placed tag). Modded traits (modStoryTraits) are NOT coord-encodable (the game assigns them coordinate order -1); activate their mod with setTraitOverlays and they apply to every scan/generate automatically. Placement (stock and modded alike): worldgen walks worlds sorted by distance from the start and the FIRST world where all of the trait's template rules fit gets it — not necessarily the start world.

tools.name: listMixingCategories
tools.description: The mixing knobs the game exposes at new-colony creation (asteroid/DLC/biome mixing). Each entry has an id (use as key in CoordFormState.mixings), an English label, the category ('dlc' / 'asteroid' / 'biome'), and levels (2 = toggle, 3 = disabled/try/guarantee).

tools.name: listModExtensions
tools.description: Workshop mods whose clusters can be scanned directly: title, Steam id, workshop URL, and each shipped cluster's coordinatePrefix + world list. Pick a cluster's prefix, build a coord with it (buildCoord works — mod prefixes are first-class), and every scan/inspect tool resolves the mod automatically. No activation step. Also lists traitOverlayMods — cluster-less mods (extra world traits, geyser packs, story-trait mods) that layer onto ANY cluster; activate those with setTraitOverlays. Each traitOverlayMods row carries storyTraits when the mod adds story traits (see listStoryTraits for their spawn tags and placement semantics), and subworldMixings when the mod adds biome remixes (Biome Remix Pack): set their levels with setTraitOverlays.

tools.name: setTraitOverlays
tools.description: Activate trait-overlay mods for THIS session. Pass the full desired set of Steam ids (empty array deactivates all). Active overlays merge into the worldgen snapshot of EVERY subsequent scan/inspect/verdict call, on top of whatever cluster the coord routes to — exactly like enabling the mods in-game. STORY-TRAIT mods (Geothermal/Demolior/Minnow) additionally apply their story trait to every generate while active (mod story traits are never coord-encodable); the trait lands on the first world by distance-from-start that fits its rules — not necessarily the start world. Valid ids come from listModExtensions' traitOverlayMods. Activation is session-lived. subworldMixings sets the levels of an active mod's biome remixes (Biome Remix Pack), keyed by settingId from listModExtensions; the coordinate can't carry them. Omitted means all Disabled. A remix the cluster's DLCs don't allow is skipped, as in-game.

steamIds.description: Complete desired activation set (replaces the previous set).

subworldMixings.description: Biome remix levels by settingId (e.g. { FrozenMixing: 'GuranteeMixing' }); Klei spells the guarantee level GuranteeMixing.

tools.name: registerCluster
tools.description: Register a custom cluster from inline worldgen YAML for THIS session. Pass the yaml files ({path, text}; paths like 'worldgen/clusters/X.yaml' or a mod folder layout — tolerant normalisation applies). The overlay must ship at least one cluster. On success the response lists each cluster's coordinatePrefix + an exampleCoord; from then on every scan/inspect/verdict tool resolves those prefixes automatically. Registration is session-lived (re-register after a server restart).

tools.name: useCgmPreset
tools.description: Register a Cluster Generation Manager (CGM) preset for THIS session. Pass the preset JSON the mod exports; it is translated into a scannable cluster under the CGM coordinate prefix. The response's baseCoord encodes the preset's own seed, story traits and mixings — scan by varying only its seed field. Re-registering replaces the previous CGM preset (one at a time, like the mod in-game).

presetJson.description: Raw preset JSON exported by the CGM mod.

tools.name: listGeysers
tools.description: Every geyser template id in the KG (28 across base + DLCs). Each entry: id, English display name, DLC gating, element output, base rate range. When `coord` is provided, entries carry per-world admissibility (which cluster worlds CAN spawn the template + which are remix-only) so you can filter before composing world.geyser or cluster.geyser constraints.

coord.description: Optional cluster coord. If given, per-world admissibility per geyser is included.

tools.name: listTraits
tools.description: Every trait id in the KG (26 across base + DLCs), PLUS traits shipped by any ACTIVE trait-overlay mod (setTraitOverlays) — those carry a fromMod marker; their admissibility is computed from the mod's own yaml. When `coord` is provided, KG entries carry per-world admissibility so you see which cluster worlds can roll each trait (random-rolled worlds only — worlds with disableWorldTraits are skipped).

tools.name: listPois
tools.description: Space POI ids (harvestable ore/organic fields, artifact fields, temporal tear). Each entry: id, English display name, DLC gating, capacity range (0..1), recharge range (0..1, lower = faster refill). No per-cluster admissibility — POIs roll per-seed from the cluster's poiPlacements, so scanning is the honest way to check availability.

tools.name: listBiomes
tools.description: Every `zoneType` value the game ships (26). These are the ids `world.biomeCount` accepts. When `coord` is provided, admissibility per world is included so you see which cluster worlds actually have each biome available.

tools.name: listWorlds
tools.description: Every world in a specific cluster: canonical path (for world.byPath refs), English label, whether it's the starting world, whether random trait rolls are disabled. Use to compose {kind: 'byPath', path: ...} WorldRef payloads without hallucination.

coord.description: Cluster coord (any seed works — worlds are shape).

tools.name: listTemplateRules
tools.description: Every worldgen template rule in a cluster, per world — the discovery palette for world.template / cluster.template constraints. Each rule lists its full template pool (the refs to constrain on), its listRule/counts/priority, and a `deterministic` flag: Guarantee* rules with a pool of 1 place identically every seed, so scanning for them is scanning for a constant — hunt Try rules, pool saturation, and WHICH pool member landed instead. Reads the same merged yamls the engine runs, so mod clusters and registered custom YAML resolve too. Story-trait stamps are not rules and never count toward template constraints.

coord.description: Cluster coord (any seed works — rules are shape).

tools.name: listConstraintKinds
tools.description: Catalog of every Builder AST constraint kind the scan tool accepts, with a one-line shape hint + minimal example. Read this ONCE when composing a new spec so you don't have to guess the payload shape. Kinds like world.geyser + poi.count carry optional output specs (uniform/tiers/sum); see the CONSTRAINT_KINDS entries.

tools.name: listSpawnTags
tools.description: Prefab-tag catalog for world.spawn / world.critter / world.plant tag or prefabId fields. IMPORTANT: constraints match these tags EXACTLY (case-sensitive) — use this tool's `query` filter (substring, case-insensitive) to find the exact tag first. Groups: 'critters' (CRITTER_IDS), 'plants' (PLANT_IDS), 'templates' (every prefab tag any worldgen template stamps — POIs, story traits, gravitas props, buried geysers — from the KG template-prefabs table, with the placing templates listed).

group.description: Restrict to critter tags, plant tags, template-placed tags, or all.

tools.name: listWorldsAcrossClusters
tools.description: Search world paths across all clusters by label substring — resolve a user's world mention ('Niobium', 'Tundra', 'Marinea') to the concrete canonical paths present in any cluster. Useful when composing world.byPath refs before you've locked a coord.

query.description: Substring match on English world name, case-insensitive.

tools.name: listHelpers
tools.description: Every ADVANCED_HELPERS function available inside preHook / postHook raw JS. Names match one-to-one with what you can call directly in a hook body. Grouped by broad domain (map, summary-world, summary-poi, summary-vanilla, geometry). Read this before writing a hook so you don't invent function names — every helper here is guaranteed to exist, and every non-listed name is guaranteed NOT to.

tools.name: listPrefabAdmissibility
tools.description: For a single prefab id + cluster coord, return admissibility per world — useful when you have a specific critter / plant / prefab in mind and want to know which cluster worlds can spawn it. Wraps worldAdmitsPrefabVerdict.

tools.name: buildCoord
tools.description: Encode a CoordFormState into a full coord string. Returns { coord, describe, validation, storyTraitWarnings }. The validation field lists any issues (invalid story trait for this cluster, DLC missing, etc.); the coord is still returned when validation warns so the caller can decide whether to proceed. storyTraitWarnings flags story-trait ids the encoder DROPPED — unknown ids, and mod story traits (which are never coord-encodable; activate their mod with setTraitOverlays instead).

storyTraits.description: STOCK story-trait ids enabled on this cluster (subset of listStoryTraits' storyTraits ids). Mod-added story traits cannot ride in a coord (the game assigns them coordinate order -1) — activate their mod via setTraitOverlays instead; unknown ids here are dropped from the coord and reported in the response's storyTraitWarnings.

mixings.description: Per-mixing-slot level: keys are MIXING_DB_ORDER entries, values 0-4 (0 = disabled).

formState.description: CoordFormState — the 4 user-controllable knobs the new-colony flow exposes.

tools.name: parseCoord
tools.description: Decode a coord string into a CoordFormState + plain-English describe. Returns null formState if the coord isn't parseable.

tools.name: describeCoord
tools.description: Plain-English readout of a coord — cluster label, seed, active story traits, mixing settings. Use to confirm a coord before spending scan time on it.

tools.name: freshCoord
tools.description: Default coord for the vanilla Sandstone Terra cluster (seed 0, no traits, no mixing). Handy starting point when the user's request doesn't specify anything.

tools.name: verdictOf
tools.description: Check whether a single Builder AST constraint is achievable at all on the given cluster. Returns {kind: 'admitted' | 'remix-only' | 'impossible', reason?} — µs check, no wasm scan. Cheap way to catch structurally-unsat constraints (e.g. 'Niobium ≤ 4 hexes from home' on a cluster where the KG places it at rings 7-10) before burning scan time.

tagSubstring.description: EXACT prefab tag (case-sensitive; the field name is historical, matching is NOT substring) compared against the world's placed entities: geyser type/tag, other_entities, buildings, pickupables. Find the exact tag with listSpawnTags (group 'templates') or listStoryTraits' spawnTag — e.g. story traits place 'MegaBrainTank', 'GravitasCreatureManipulator', 'GeothermalVentEntity' (mod). Story traits land on the FIRST world by distance-from-start that fits all their rules, not necessarily the start world. templates.description: Full worldgen template refs, EXACT match against the wasm's placed templates (e.g. 'poi/frozen/heatsink_a', 'expansion1::geysers/molten_aluminum'). tools.name: scan
tools.description:
Scan a seed range against a Builder AST spec and return top-K matches. Tier auto-
selected from the AST — bytecode (~1M seeds/sec/core) for require-mode +
bytecode-capable constraints; JS (~50k/sec/core) for prefer mode or map-tier
constraints. Within JS, geyser-family constraints (world/cluster.geyser,
world/cluster.oilWells, home.geyserNearStart) run PARTIAL worldgen — one
worldgen.partials() call per seed covering only the referenced worlds, geyser
output identical to a full generate (measured ~80ms vs ~250ms per seed on a
9-world cluster). Any cell-reading constraint (sussy/trash/biomeCount/
elementMass/spawn/critter/plant/marshy/niobium) promotes the whole spec to full
worldgen (~250-500ms per seed) — the partial constraints then reuse that map, so
one generation per seed either way.

STREAMING: JS-tier scans emit notifications/progress every ~1s wall time when the
client opts in via _meta.progressToken. Each notification carries running counts +
the current leader; the final response also includes a top-level `cancelled` flag.
Cancel-request (JSON-RPC) is honored — server returns the top-K accumulated so far.

PATTERN — cheap-gate + expensive-gate: when combining a summary-tier require
(world.trait, poi.count, world.distToHome) with a map-tier require (world.geyser,
world.biomeCount, etc.), put BOTH in the spec — compile-to-js orders them so the
summary gate short-circuits before worldgen fires. E.g. 'GeoActive + salt_water>=3'
on 5000 seeds runs in ~8 min instead of ~40 because only Geoactive seeds (~10%) pay
the worldgen cost. The response's tier.stats {seedsScanned, seedsPassed,
seedsRanWorldgen} reveals how well this short-circuit worked; if seedsRanWorldgen
is close to seedsScanned, your summary gate isn't cutting anything.

Response contract: `spec.rules` is a plain-English readout of what was scanned for
(quote directly to the user). `results[i].columns[j]` carries diagnostic values —
combined with `sortBy: 'column:<name>'`, that's often the real ranking, not score.
Impossible require constraints are caught BEFORE the scan runs (see verdictOfSpec);
response is `isError: true` with a specific reason.

constraints.description: Builder AST constraint list. v0.4 covers every kind the web app builder supports: world.trait, world.geyser, world.distToHome, world.distTo, world.traitCount, world.oilWells, world.critter, world.plant, world.spawn, world.biomeCount, world.marshyTungstenInMagma, world.niobiumVolcanoAccess, world.sussy, world.trash, world.asteroidRemix, poi.count, map.elementMass, home.geyserNearStart, cluster.geyser, cluster.oilWells, cluster.critter, cluster.plant, cluster.spawn, cluster.sussy, cluster.trash. Call listConstraintKinds (v0.5) for the shape catalog.

preHook.description: v0.6 raw-JS escape hatch. Runs BEFORE Builder requires. Can `return {pass: false}` to skip a seed cheaper than any AST constraint. Async-first: top-level `await worldgen()` works, and an async `{pass: false}` gates the seed. Keep the cheap summary checks (hasTrait etc.) BEFORE the first await so rejected seeds never pay the worldgen cost. Store computed values on `scratch` (per-seed {}) for the postHook to turn into a score. Bindings: summary, seed, worldgen, col, scratch, plus every ADVANCED_HELPERS function (call listHelpers). Forces JS-tier (bytecode won't run). Must not shadow reserved names.

postHook.description: v0.6 raw-JS escape hatch. Runs AFTER Builder prefers + col() emissions. Reads and can mutate `score` — THE way to rank hook-computed values (set score here, then sort by score; often from values the preHook stashed on `scratch`). Top-level `await` works. Can call col() to add its own diagnostic. Returning is a no-op — the tool re-emits the final return. Forces JS-tier.

hooksTier.description: Declares what the hooks await: 'summary' (no worldgen calls), 'partial-worldgen' (awaits worldgenPartial), or 'worldgen' (awaits full worldgen()). The declaration drives the tier expectation in the response envelope instead of source-sniffing; a hook that plainly contradicts its declaration is rejected upfront. Omit only for legacy callers — then the tier is inferred from the hook text.

spec.description: Query spec — Builder AST (+ optional raw-JS hooks).

sortBy.description: Sort key. 'score' (default) → highest score first. 'column:<name>' → sort by a col() diagnostic value (e.g. 'column:home_salt_water_geyser'). For bytecode-tier scans the wasm already narrowed to top-K by SCORE before we see the results, so 'column:' just re-sorts that top-K — if you want true column ranking across the full range, use JS-tier (add prefer-mode or map-tier constraints).

opts.description: Scan range + top-K cap + sort. For map-tier scans (world.geyser etc.), prefer seedRangeEnd <= 10_000 or expect multi-minute latency.

tools.name: scanUntil
tools.description: Streaming scan that terminates as soon as `targetHits` seeds match the spec (or the seed range is exhausted, or the caller cancels). Right for 'find me N seeds with X' where you don't need the exhaustive top-K — stops early to save time. Emits notifications/progress every ~1s wall time when the client opts in via _meta.progressToken. Response has `stopReason` ∈ {'targetHits reached', 'cancelled', 'range exhausted'} — the single stop-signal to narrate. Cancel-request returns whatever's accumulated so far.

tools.name: getSeedSummary
tools.description: Summary-tier seed inspection (~5ms). Returns cluster summary (worlds + distances + per-world traits) and grouped POI counts with capacity/recharge roll ranges. Enough for POI/trait drill-down without running worldgen. For geyser rates + positions, use getSeedDeep (much slower).

seed.description: Optional seed override — if the coord already carries the seed you want, omit this.

tools.name: getSeedDeep
tools.description: Deep seed inspection (~500ms — runs full worldgen). Per-world geyser types + year-avg kg/s + positions, oil well counts, total geyser count. Use when the LLM needs to explain WHY a scan result ranked where it did.

tools.name: describeSeed
tools.description: Plain-English seed narration. `deep: false` (default) runs summary-only (~5ms); `deep: true` runs worldgen (~500ms) so geyser rates + oil wells appear in the narration. Quote the `describe` field directly to the user without parsing JSON.

tools.name: shareResults
tools.description:
Hand off an MCP-driven hunt to the web app. Encodes {coord, spec.constraints, seeds} into a shareable payload, uploads via the web app's existing share endpoint (R2-backed, CDN-cached), and returns the URL. The user opens the URL → sussy-seeds hydrates the Builder tab with the exact spec, pins the seeds under the coord's prefix, and populates the coord. Session continues where MCP left off — same leaderboard, editable constraints, no re-typing.

Use at the END of a productive hunt to give the user a persistent artifact they can share, bookmark, or return to. Cheap — one POST per share, edge-cached forever. Not for every scan; call it when the results are worth revisiting.

tagSubstring.description: EXACT prefab tag (case-sensitive; the field name is historical, matching is NOT substring), summed across every world in the cluster — the cluster-wide form of world.spawn. Find tags via listSpawnTags (group 'templates').

templates.description: Full worldgen template refs, EXACT match against the wasm's placed templates (e.g. 'poi/frozen/heatsink_a', 'expansion1::geysers/molten_aluminum'). One ref = did that template stamp; a rule's whole pool = how many times the rule fired regardless of which member it rolled — the lever world.spawn can't reach when pool members place identical prefabs. Discover refs + pools via listTemplateRules. Story-trait stamps are never counted (partial worldgen skips them) — use world.spawn for those.
world.template summed across every world in the cluster (exact template-ref match; story-trait stamps never counted).

prefabId.description: Match specific critter prefab (e.g. 'Pacu'). Omit for any critter.
Match specific plant prefab (e.g. 'GasGrass'). Omit for any plant.

mixingSlot.description: Mixing slot id from MIXING_DB_ORDER, e.g. 'CeresAsteroidMixing', 'PrehistoricAsteroidMixing', 'AquaticAsteroidMixing'.

preHook.description: Optional raw JS spliced BEFORE Builder requires (see v0.6 hooks). Ships in the share payload; hydrates onto the Builder tab's JS-hooks card in the web app. Setting either hook forces the JS tier.

postHook.description: Optional raw JS spliced AFTER Builder prefers + col() emits. Reads / mutates score, can call col(). Must NOT return.

seeds.description: Seeds to pin — typically the top-K from a scan or a hand-picked short list. Max 200 (web app share limit).

scanLimit.description: Range end the MCP scan used, or null to leave unset. The web app renders it as the resume-scan cap.

tab.description: Which sussy-seeds tab the user lands on. 'builder' is the default (matches the AST-shaped spec MCP composes). 'advanced' if you're shipping raw JS in `source`.

source.description: Override for the `source` field. For tab='builder' (default) we auto-emit `JSON.stringify({constraints})`; pass this to override (e.g. when tab='advanced' and you want to hand off a raw JS body).

tools.name: probeStreaming
tools.description: Diagnostic: emit N progress notifications spaced by delayMs, then return. Use to verify what your MCP client does with notifications/progress — whether they surface into the LLM's context, render in a status area, or get swallowed. Not for real hunts.

steps.description: Number of progress notifications to emit.

tools.name: ping
tools.description: Smoke test — returns 'pong' with the server version. Use to verify the MCP connection is live before running a real scan.

tools.name: probeSummarize
tools.description: Diagnostic — boots the gambling wasm and returns the full ClusterSummary for one cluster_seed on the given coord. Confirms end-to-end that the scanner works. Not intended for LLM-driven discovery; the real scan tool lands in a follow-up.

instructions: MCP server for Oxygen Not Included seed hunting. Compose a scan by picking a cluster (listClusters → buildCoord) and a Builder AST spec (listConstraintKinds for shapes), then call scan. Every scan response includes a plain-English rules readout. Modded clusters scan too: listModExtensions for Workshop mods (their coord prefixes are first-class everywhere), registerCluster to scan inline custom worldgen YAML — sources resolve by coord prefix, no activation step. Geyser- and template-family specs run partial worldgen (only the referenced worlds generate) automatically.
